claim: Obesity is associated with blunted β-adrenoreceptor (β-AR)-mediated lipolysis and lipid oxidation in adipose tissue.
source: Obesity is associated with blunted β-adrenoreceptor (β-AR)-mediated lipolysis and lipid oxidation in adipose tissue, but the mechanisms linking nutrient overload to catecholamine resistance are poorly understood.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research (Reynisdottir et al., 1994; Arner, 1999; Jocken et al., 2008) mentioned later in the manuscript.

claim: Targeted disruption of ALK7 alleviates diet-induced catecholamine resistance in adipose tissue.
source: We report that targeted disruption of TGF-β superfamily receptor ALK7 alleviates diet-induced catecholamine resistance in adipose tissue, thereby reducing obesity in mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from knockout mice presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out enhanced adipose β-AR expression under a high fat diet.
source: Global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out enhanced adipose β-AR expression, β-adrenergic signaling, mitochondrial biogenesis, lipid oxidation, and lipolysis under a high fat diet, leading to elevated energy expenditure, decreased fat mass, and resistance to diet-induced obesity.
evidence: This is supported by Q-PCR data showing increased Adrb1 and Adrb3 mRNA levels in knockout mice (Figure 5E-I).

claim: Global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out enhanced β-adrenergic signaling under a high fat diet.
source: Global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out enhanced adipose β-AR expression, β-adrenergic signaling, mitochondrial biogenesis, lipid oxidation, and lipolysis under a high fat diet, leading to elevated energy expenditure, decreased fat mass, and resistance to diet-induced obesity.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data showing increased phosphorylated HSL and PKA substrates (Figure 5J-L).

claim: Global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out enhanced mitochondrial biogenesis under a high fat diet.
source: Global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out enhanced adipose β-AR expression, β-adrenergic signaling, mitochondrial biogenesis, lipid oxidation, and lipolysis under a high fat diet, leading to elevated energy expenditure, decreased fat mass, and resistance to diet-induced obesity.
evidence: This is supported by measurements of mitochondrial DNA content, citrate synthase activity, and ATP content (Figure 4A-F).

claim: Global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out enhanced lipid oxidation under a high fat diet.
source: Global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out enhanced adipose β-AR expression, β-adrenergic signaling, mitochondrial biogenesis, lipid oxidation, and lipolysis under a high fat diet, leading to elevated energy expenditure, decreased fat mass, and resistance to diet-induced obesity.
evidence: This is supported by lipid oxidation assays in adipose tissue (Figure 4I-J).

claim: Global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out enhanced lipolysis under a high fat diet.
source: Global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out enhanced adipose β-AR expression, β-adrenergic signaling, mitochondrial biogenesis, lipid oxidation, and lipolysis under a high fat diet, leading to elevated energy expenditure, decreased fat mass, and resistance to diet-induced obesity.
evidence: This is supported by lipolysis assays showing increased free fatty acid release (Figure 5A-C).

claim: Global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out led to elevated energy expenditure under a high fat diet.
source: Global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out enhanced adipose β-AR expression, β-adrenergic signaling, mitochondrial biogenesis, lipid oxidation, and lipolysis under a high fat diet, leading to elevated energy expenditure, decreased fat mass, and resistance to diet-induced obesity.
evidence: This is supported by calorimetric measurements (Figure 3A-B).

claim: Global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out led to decreased fat mass under a high fat diet.
source: Global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out enhanced adipose β-AR expression, β-adrenergic signaling, mitochondrial biogenesis, lipid oxidation, and lipolysis under a high fat diet, leading to elevated energy expenditure, decreased fat mass, and resistance to diet-induced obesity.
evidence: This is supported by MRI measurements and fat depot weights (Figure 1D-H).

claim: Global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out led to resistance to diet-induced obesity.
source: Global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out enhanced adipose β-AR expression, β-adrenergic signaling, mitochondrial biogenesis, lipid oxidation, and lipolysis under a high fat diet, leading to elevated energy expenditure, decreased fat mass, and resistance to diet-induced obesity.
evidence: This is supported by weight gain measurements (Figure 1A-B).

claim: Activation of ALK7 reduced β-AR-mediated signaling in mouse adipocytes.
source: Conversely, activation of ALK7 reduced β-AR-mediated signaling and lipolysis cell-autonomously in both mouse and human adipocytes.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data showing reduced phosphorylation of HSL and PKA substrates after activin B treatment (Figure 6E-F).

claim: Activation of ALK7 reduced lipolysis in mouse adipocytes.
source: Conversely, activation of ALK7 reduced β-AR-mediated signaling and lipolysis cell-autonomously in both mouse and human adipocytes.
evidence: This is supported by lipolysis assays in MEF-derived adipocytes treated with activin B (Figure 6G-H).

claim: Activation of ALK7 reduced β-AR-mediated signaling in human adipocytes.
source: Conversely, activation of ALK7 reduced β-AR-mediated signaling and lipolysis cell-autonomously in both mouse and human adipocytes.
evidence: This is inferred from the lipolysis data in human adipocytes showing reduced response to isoproterenol after activin B treatment (Figure 6I-J).

claim: Activation of ALK7 reduced lipolysis in human adipocytes.
source: Conversely, activation of ALK7 reduced β-AR-mediated signaling and lipolysis cell-autonomously in both mouse and human adipocytes.
evidence: This is supported by lipolysis assays in human adipocytes treated with activin B or ALK7 overexpression (Figure 6I-J).

claim: Acute inhibition of ALK7 in adult mice reduced diet-induced weight gain.
source: Acute inhibition of ALK7 in adult mice by a chemical-genetic approach reduced diet-induced weight gain, fat accumulation, and adipocyte size, and enhanced adipocyte lipolysis and β-adrenergic signaling.
evidence: This is supported by weight measurements in Alk7ASKA mice treated with 1NaPP1 (Figure 7C).

claim: Acute inhibition of ALK7 in adult mice reduced fat accumulation.
source: Acute inhibition of ALK7 in adult mice by a chemical-genetic approach reduced diet-induced weight gain, fat accumulation, and adipocyte size, and enhanced adipocyte lipolysis and β-adrenergic signaling.
evidence: This is supported by fat depot weight measurements in Alk7ASKA mice treated with 1NaPP1 (Figure 7E).

claim: Acute inhibition of ALK7 in adult mice reduced adipocyte size.
source: Acute inhibition of ALK7 in adult mice by a chemical-genetic approach reduced diet-induced weight gain, fat accumulation, and adipocyte size, and enhanced adipocyte lipolysis and β-adrenergic signaling.
evidence: This is supported by histological analysis of adipocyte cell size (Figure 7G-H).

claim: Acute inhibition of ALK7 in adult mice enhanced adipocyte lipolysis.
source: Acute inhibition of ALK7 in adult mice by a chemical-genetic approach reduced diet-induced weight gain, fat accumulation, and adipocyte size, and enhanced adipocyte lipolysis and β-adrenergic signaling.
evidence: This is supported by lipolysis assays in adipose tissue biopsies from 1NaPP1-treated mice (Figure 8A).

claim: Acute inhibition of ALK7 in adult mice enhanced β-adrenergic signaling.
source: Acute inhibition of ALK7 in adult mice by a chemical-genetic approach reduced diet-induced weight gain, fat accumulation, and adipocyte size, and enhanced adipocyte lipolysis and β-adrenergic signaling.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data showing increased phosphorylated HSL and PKA substrates (Figure 8C-E).

claim: ALK7 signaling contributes to diet-induced catecholamine resistance in adipose tissue.
source: We propose that ALK7 signaling contributes to diet-induced catecholamine resistance in adipose tissue, and suggest that ALK7 inhibitors may have therapeutic value in human obesity.
evidence: This is based on the collective experimental data showing that ALK7 disruption prevents catecholamine resistance.

claim: ALK7 inhibitors may have therapeutic value in human obesity.
source: We propose that ALK7 signaling contributes to diet-induced catecholamine resistance in adipose tissue, and suggest that ALK7 inhibitors may have therapeutic value in human obesity.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal based on the experimental findings in mice and human adipocytes.

claim: β3-adrenoceptor agonists are effective anti-obesity agents in rodents.
source: Agonists of β3-adrenoceptors (β3-AR) are effective anti-obesity agents in rodents due to their ability to stimulate lipolysis and lipid oxidation in adipose tissue (Arch, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Arch, 2011.

claim: β3-adrenoceptor agonists stimulate lipolysis in rodent adipose tissue.
source: Agonists of β3-adrenoceptors (β3-AR) are effective anti-obesity agents in rodents due to their ability to stimulate lipolysis and lipid oxidation in adipose tissue (Arch, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Arch, 2011.

claim: β3-adrenoceptor agonists stimulate lipid oxidation in rodent adipose tissue.
source: Agonists of β3-adrenoceptors (β3-AR) are effective anti-obesity agents in rodents due to their ability to stimulate lipolysis and lipid oxidation in adipose tissue (Arch, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Arch, 2011.

claim: The pharmacology of rodent and human β3-AR differs.
source: However, efforts to develop similar compounds in humans stalled when it became clear that the pharmacology of rodent and human β3-AR differed and lipolysis in human adipocytes was mainly mediated by classical β1- and β2-AR, which can also induce hypertension, tachycardia, and other undesired complications (Arch, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Arch, 2011.

claim: Lipolysis in human adipocytes is mainly mediated by β1- and β2-AR.
source: However, efforts to develop similar compounds in humans stalled when it became clear that the pharmacology of rodent and human β3-AR differed and lipolysis in human adipocytes was mainly mediated by classical β1- and β2-AR, which can also induce hypertension, tachycardia, and other undesired complications (Arch, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Arch, 2011.

claim: β1- and β2-AR agonists can induce hypertension, tachycardia, and other undesired complications.
source: However, efforts to develop similar compounds in humans stalled when it became clear that the pharmacology of rodent and human β3-AR differed and lipolysis in human adipocytes was mainly mediated by classical β1- and β2-AR, which can also induce hypertension, tachycardia, and other undesired complications (Arch, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Arch, 2011.

claim: In both humans and rodents, obesity is associated with blunted β-AR-mediated lipolysis in adipose tissue.
source: In both humans and rodents, obesity is associated with blunted β-AR-mediated lipolysis and lipid oxidation in adipose tissue (Reynisdottir et al., 1994; Arner, 1999; Jocken et al., 2008), but the mechanisms linking nutrient overload to catecholamine resistance remain poorly understood.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Reynisdottir et al., 1994; Arner, 1999; Jocken et al., 2008.

claim: In both humans and rodents, obesity is associated with blunted lipid oxidation in adipose tissue.
source: In both humans and rodents, obesity is associated with blunted β-AR-mediated lipolysis and lipid oxidation in adipose tissue (Reynisdottir et al., 1994; Arner, 1999; Jocken et al., 2008), but the mechanisms linking nutrient overload to catecholamine resistance remain poorly understood.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Reynisdottir et al., 1994; Arner, 1999; Jocken et al., 2008.

claim: ALK7 is a receptor for Nodal.
source: ALK7 is a receptor for a subset of ligands from the TGF-β superfamily, including Nodal, activin B, and GDF-3 (Rydén et al., 1996; Reissmann et al., 2001; Tsuchida et al., 2004; Andersson et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Rydén et al., 1996; Reissmann et al., 2001; Tsuchida et al., 2004; Andersson et al., 2008.

claim: ALK7 is a receptor for activin B.
source: ALK7 is a receptor for a subset of ligands from the TGF-β superfamily, including Nodal, activin B, and GDF-3 (Rydén et al., 1996; Reissmann et al., 2001; Tsuchida et al., 2004; Andersson et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Rydén et al., 1996; Reissmann et al., 2001; Tsuchida et al., 2004; Andersson et al., 2008.

claim: ALK7 is a receptor for GDF-3.
source: ALK7 is a receptor for a subset of ligands from the TGF-β superfamily, including Nodal, activin B, and GDF-3 (Rydén et al., 1996; Reissmann et al., 2001; Tsuchida et al., 2004; Andersson et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Rydén et al., 1996; Reissmann et al., 2001; Tsuchida et al., 2004; Andersson et al., 2008.

claim: ALK7 is not necessary for mouse embryogenesis.
source: ALK7 is not necessary for mouse embryogenesis (Jörnvall et al., 2004), suggesting alternative functions in postnatal development and adult physiology.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jörnvall et al., 2004.

claim: ALK7 is highly expressed in rodent adipose tissue.
source: ALK7 is highly expressed in rodent and human adipose tissue (Kang and Reddi, 1996; Andersson et al., 2008; Carlsson et al., 2009; Murakami et al., 2012), as well as in a few other tissues implicated in metabolic regulation, such as pancreatic islets (Bertolino et al., 2008) and the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus (Sandoval-Guzmán et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kang and Reddi, 1996; Andersson et al., 2008; Carlsson et al., 2009; Murakami et al., 2012.

claim: ALK7 is highly expressed in human adipose tissue.
source: ALK7 is highly expressed in rodent and human adipose tissue (Kang and Reddi, 1996; Andersson et al., 2008; Carlsson et al., 2009; Murakami et al., 2012), as well as in a few other tissues implicated in metabolic regulation, such as pancreatic islets (Bertolino et al., 2008) and the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus (Sandoval-Guzmán et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kang and Reddi, 1996; Andersson et al., 2008; Carlsson et al., 2009; Murakami et al., 2012.

claim: ALK7 is expressed in pancreatic islets.
source: ALK7 is highly expressed in rodent and human adipose tissue (Kang and Reddi, 1996; Andersson et al., 2008; Carlsson et al., 2009; Murakami et al., 2012), as well as in a few other tissues implicated in metabolic regulation, such as pancreatic islets (Bertolino et al., 2008) and the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus (Sandoval-Guzmán et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bertolino et al., 2008.

claim: ALK7 is expressed in the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus.
source: ALK7 is highly expressed in rodent and human adipose tissue (Kang and Reddi, 1996; Andersson et al., 2008; Carlsson et al., 2009; Murakami et al., 2012), as well as in a few other tissues implicated in metabolic regulation, such as pancreatic islets (Bertolino et al., 2008) and the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus (Sandoval-Guzmán et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sandoval-Guzmán et al., 2012.

claim: Mice lacking ALK7 show reduced fat accumulation after a high fat diet.
source: Mice lacking ALK7 show reduced fat accumulation after a high fat diet (Andersson et al., 2008) and in a polygenic model of obesity (Yogosawa et al., 2013), but the mechanisms underlying the effects of ALK7 signaling on diet-induced obesity are not understood.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Andersson et al., 2008.

claim: Mice lacking ALK7 show reduced fat accumulation in a polygenic model of obesity.
source: Mice lacking ALK7 show reduced fat accumulation after a high fat diet (Andersson et al., 2008) and in a polygenic model of obesity (Yogosawa et al., 2013), but the mechanisms underlying the effects of ALK7 signaling on diet-induced obesity are not understood.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yogosawa et al., 2013.

claim: Pancreatic islets from Alk7 knock-out mice show enhanced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion.
source: Pancreatic islets from Alk7 knock-out mice show enhanced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (Bertolino et al., 2008), a phenotype that is also present in islets from mutant mice lacking the ALK7 ligand activin B (Wu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bertolino et al., 2008.

claim: Pancreatic islets from mutant mice lacking activin B show enhanced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion.
source: Pancreatic islets from Alk7 knock-out mice show enhanced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (Bertolino et al., 2008), a phenotype that is also present in islets from mutant mice lacking the ALK7 ligand activin B (Wu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wu et al., 2014.

claim: The arcuate nucleus of Alk7 knock-out mice shows reduced expression of Npy mRNA compared to wild type controls.
source: Moreover, the arcuate nucleus of Alk7 knock-out mice shows reduced expression of Npy mRNA and lower numbers of Npy-expressing neurons compared to wild type controls (Sandoval-Guzmán et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sandoval-Guzmán et al., 2012.

claim: The arcuate nucleus of Alk7 knock-out mice shows lower numbers of Npy-expressing neurons compared to wild type controls.
source: Moreover, the arcuate nucleus of Alk7 knock-out mice shows reduced expression of Npy mRNA and lower numbers of Npy-expressing neurons compared to wild type controls (Sandoval-Guzmán et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sandoval-Guzmán et al., 2012.

claim: A conditional knock-out allele of the mouse Alk7 gene was generated with loxP sites flanking exons 5 and 6.
source: In order to dissect the cell-autonomous functions of ALK7 in specific tissues, we generated a conditional knock-out allele of the mouse Alk7 gene (also known as Acvr1c) with loxP sites flanking exons 5 and 6, encoding essential regions of the ALK7 kinase domain (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the description in the text and the schematic in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Exons 5 and 6 of Alk7 encode essential regions of the ALK7 kinase domain.
source: In order to dissect the cell-autonomous functions of ALK7 in specific tissues, we generated a conditional knock-out allele of the mouse Alk7 gene (also known as Acvr1c) with loxP sites flanking exons 5 and 6, encoding essential regions of the ALK7 kinase domain (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Gene deletion in adipose tissue was achieved by crossing Alk7fx mice with Ap2CRE mice.
source: Gene deletion in adipose tissue was achieved by crossing Alk7fx mice with Ap2CRE mice (He et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method used.

claim: Ap2CRE has been reported to be expressed in adipose tissue macrophages.
source: Although Ap2CRE has also been reported to be expressed in adipose tissue macrophages (Lee et al., 2013), Alk7 mRNA expression could only be detected in the adipocyte fraction of adipose tissue but not in the stromal-vascular fraction (containing macrophages) or in spleen (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lee et al., 2013.

claim: Alk7 mRNA expression could only be detected in the adipocyte fraction of adipose tissue but not in the stromal-vascular fraction or in spleen.
source: Although Ap2CRE has also been reported to be expressed in adipose tissue macrophages (Lee et al., 2013), Alk7 mRNA expression could only be detected in the adipocyte fraction of adipose tissue but not in the stromal-vascular fraction (containing macrophages) or in spleen (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: This is supported by Q-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-D.

claim: Expression of Alk7 mRNA was reduced by 60% in the adipose tissue of Alk7fx/fx::Ap2CRE mice.
source: Expression of Alk7 mRNA was reduced by 60% in the adipose tissue of Alk7fx/fx::Ap2CRE mice, while a 98% reduction was achieved in Alk7fx/−::Ap2CRE mice (i.e., compound heterozygotes carrying floxed and knock-out Alk7 alleles) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by Q-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Expression of Alk7 mRNA was reduced by 98% in the adipose tissue of Alk7fx/−::Ap2CRE mice.
source: Expression of Alk7 mRNA was reduced by 60% in the adipose tissue of Alk7fx/fx::Ap2CRE mice, while a 98% reduction was achieved in Alk7fx/−::Ap2CRE mice (i.e., compound heterozygotes carrying floxed and knock-out Alk7 alleles) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by Q-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: No change in Alk7 mRNA expression was observed in the pancreas or brain of fat-specific Alk7 mutant mice.
source: No change in Alk7 mRNA expression was observed in the pancreas or brain (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by Q-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Both lines of fat-specific Alk7 mutant mice showed significantly reduced weight gain during 12 weeks on a high fat diet compared to controls.
source: Both lines of fat-specific Alk7 mutant mice showed significantly reduced weight gain during 12 weeks on a high fat diet compared to controls (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by weight gain data shown in Figure 1A-B.

claim: Weight gain in Alk7fx/fx::NestinCRE mice did not differ from controls.
source: In contrast, weight gain in Alk7fx/fx::NestinCRE mice, lacking ALK7 expression in the nervous system (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C), did not differ from controls (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by weight gain data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Diet-induced fat accumulation was significantly reduced in fat-specific Alk7 mutant mice compared to controls as measured by epididymal and retroperitoneal fat depot weight.
source: Diet-induced fat accumulation, as measured by epididymal and retroperitoneal fat depot weight (Figure 1D–F), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of total fat mass (Figure 1G,H), and adipocyte cell size (Figure 1I,J), was also significantly reduced in fat-specific Alk7 mutant mice compared to controls.
evidence: This is supported by fat depot weight measurements shown in Figure 1D-F.

claim: Diet-induced fat accumulation was significantly reduced in fat-specific Alk7 mutant mice compared to controls as measured by MRI of total fat mass.
source: Diet-induced fat accumulation, as measured by epididymal and retroperitoneal fat depot weight (Figure 1D–F), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of total fat mass (Figure 1G,H), and adipocyte cell size (Figure 1I,J), was also significantly reduced in fat-specific Alk7 mutant mice compared to controls.
evidence: This is supported by MRI data shown in Figure 1G-H.

claim: Diet-induced fat accumulation was significantly reduced in fat-specific Alk7 mutant mice compared to controls as measured by adipocyte cell size.
source: Diet-induced fat accumulation, as measured by epididymal and retroperitoneal fat depot weight (Figure 1D–F), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of total fat mass (Figure 1G,H), and adipocyte cell size (Figure 1I,J), was also significantly reduced in fat-specific Alk7 mutant mice compared to controls.
evidence: This is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 1I-J.

claim: Fat depots of nervous system-specific Alk7 mutant mice were not different from controls.
source: In contrast, fat depots of nervous system-specific Alk7 mutant mice were not different from controls (Figure 1K).
evidence: This is supported by fat depot weight measurements shown in Figure 1K.

claim: Serum leptin levels were lower after a high fat diet in both global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out mice.
source: In agreement with reduced diet-induced obesity, serum leptin levels were also lower after a high fat diet in both global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out mice (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is supported by serum leptin measurements shown in Figure 2A-B.

claim: Fed serum insulin levels remained unchanged in fat-specific Alk7 knock-out mice.
source: However, fed serum insulin levels remained unchanged in fat-specific and brain-specific Alk7 knock-out mice (Figure 2C,D), suggesting unaltered peripheral insulin sensitivity.
evidence: This is supported by serum insulin measurements shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Fed serum insulin levels remained unchanged in brain-specific Alk7 knock-out mice.
source: However, fed serum insulin levels remained unchanged in fat-specific and brain-specific Alk7 knock-out mice (Figure 2C,D), suggesting unaltered peripheral insulin sensitivity.
evidence: This is supported by serum insulin measurements shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Glucose and insulin tolerance tests performed in fat-specific Alk7 mutant mice indicated normal glucose and insulin responses in the mutants.
source: In addition, glucose and insulin tolerance tests performed in fat-specific Alk7 mutant mice and controls indicated normal glucose and insulin responses in the mutants (Figure 2E–H).
evidence: This is supported by glucose and insulin tolerance test data shown in Figure 2E-H.

claim: Obesity has been associated with a state of inflammation in adipose tissue in which resident macrophages play important roles.
source: Obesity has been associated with a state of inflammation in adipose tissue in which resident macrophages play important roles (Hotamisligil, 2006; Fujisaka et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hotamisligil, 2006; Fujisaka et al., 2009.

claim: Following 8 weeks of a high fat diet, adipose tissue of global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out mice showed decreased expression of markers of pro-inflammatory M1 macrophages.
source: Following 8 weeks of a high fat diet, adipose tissue of global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out mice showed decreased expression of markers of pro-inflammatory M1 macrophages, such as TNF1α, IL-12b, and Itgax (Figure 2I,J), but increased expression of Mgl2, a marker of M2 macrophages, the major resident macrophages involved in remodeling and repair that are normally present in adipose tissue from lean mice (Figure 2K,L).
evidence: This is supported by Q-PCR data shown in Figure 2I-J.

claim: Following 8 weeks of a high fat diet, adipose tissue of global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out mice showed increased expression of Mgl2, a marker of M2 macrophages.
source: Following 8 weeks of a high fat diet, adipose tissue of global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out mice showed decreased expression of markers of pro-inflammatory M1 macrophages, such as TNF1α, IL-12b, and Itgax (Figure 2I,J), but increased expression of Mgl2, a marker of M2 macrophages, the major resident macrophages involved in remodeling and repair that are normally present in adipose tissue from lean mice (Figure 2K,L).
evidence: This is supported by Q-PCR data shown in Figure 2K-L.

claim: M2 macrophages are the major resident macrophages involved in remodeling and repair that are normally present in adipose tissue from lean mice.
source: Following 8 weeks of a high fat diet, adipose tissue of global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out mice showed decreased expression of markers of pro-inflammatory M1 macrophages, such as TNF1α, IL-12b, and Itgax (Figure 2I,J), but increased expression of Mgl2, a marker of M2 macrophages, the major resident macrophages involved in remodeling and repair that are normally present in adipose tissue from lean mice (Figure 2K,L).
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about macrophage subtypes.

claim: ALK7 functions cell-autonomously in adipose tissue to regulate fat accumulation during nutrient overload.
source: Together, these results indicate that ALK7 functions cell-autonomously in adipose tissue to regulate fat accumulation during nutrient overload.
evidence: This is an inference based on the collective data from fat-specific knockout mice.

claim: Both global knock-out and fat-specific Alk7 mutant mice displayed increased energy expenditure after a high fat diet compared to controls.
source: Both global knock-out and fat-specific Alk7 mutant mice displayed increased energy expenditure (Figure 3A,B) and oxygen consumption (Figure 3C,D) after a high fat diet compared to controls.
evidence: This is supported by calorimetric measurements shown in Figure 3A-B.

claim: Both global knock-out and fat-specific Alk7 mutant mice displayed increased oxygen consumption after a high fat diet compared to controls.
source: Both global knock-out and fat-specific Alk7 mutant mice displayed increased energy expenditure (Figure 3A,B) and oxygen consumption (Figure 3C,D) after a high fat diet compared to controls.
evidence: This is supported by oxygen consumption measurements shown in Figure 3C-D.

claim: Food intake remained unchanged in Alk7 mutant mice.
source: Food intake remained unchanged in the mutant mice (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by food intake measurements shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Changes in energy expenditure in Alk7 mutant mice were not due to 'browning' of subcutaneous adipose tissue.
source: Changes in energy expenditure in Alk7 mutant mice were not due to 'browning' of subcutaneous adipose tissue, as expression of brown adipose tissue (BAT) marker genes Ucp1 and Elovl3 was not increased in the subcutaneous fat of the mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by Q-PCR data showing no increase in BAT markers in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: Expression of brown adipose tissue marker genes Ucp1 and Elovl3 was not increased in the subcutaneous fat of Alk7 mutant mice.
source: Changes in energy expenditure in Alk7 mutant mice were not due to 'browning' of subcutaneous adipose tissue, as expression of brown adipose tissue (BAT) marker genes Ucp1 and Elovl3 was not increased in the subcutaneous fat of the mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by Q-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: The browning effects of the β3-AR-specific agonist CL316243 were comparable in subcutaneous adipose tissue of wild type and Alk7 knock-out mice.
source: Moreover, the browning effects of the β3-AR-specific agonist CL316243 were comparable in subcutaneous adipose tissue of wild type and Alk7 knock-out mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is supported by Q-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C-D.

claim: Expression of BAT markers was not elevated in the BAT of Alk7 mutant mice.
source: Neither was expression of BAT markers elevated in the BAT of Alk7 mutant mice (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the text but data is not shown.

claim: Global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out mice showed higher physical activity than wild type controls after a high fat diet.
source: Global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out mice showed higher physical activity than wild type controls after a high fat diet (Figure 3F,G).
evidence: This is supported by ambulation measurements shown in Figure 3F-G.

claim: Changes in activity do not drive changes in energy expenditure in groups of mice below thermoneutrality.
source: However, it was recently reported that changes in activity do not drive changes in energy expenditure in groups of mice below thermoneutrality (Virtue et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Virtue et al., 2012.

claim: Mitochondria biogenesis is impaired by chronic nutrient overload in rodents and humans.
source: We hypothesized that increased energy expenditure in Alk7 mutant mice on a high fat diet may be due to higher basal metabolic rate, and investigated adipose tissue mitochondria biogenesis and function, which are impaired by chronic nutrient overload in rodents and humans (Heilbronn et al., 2007; Rong et al., 2007; Sutherland et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Heilbronn et al., 2007; Rong et al., 2007; Sutherland et al., 2008.

claim: Mitochondria biogenesis was significantly increased in adipose tissue of both global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out mice on a high fat diet compared to controls as measured by mitochondrial DNA content.
source: Mitochondria biogenesis, as measured by mitochondrial DNA content (Figure 4A,B), citrate synthase activity (Figure 4C,D), and ATP content (Figure 4E,F), was significantly increased in adipose tissue of both global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out mice on a high fat diet compared to controls.
evidence: This is supported by mitochondrial DNA measurements shown in Figure 4A-B.

claim: Mitochondria biogenesis was significantly increased in adipose tissue of both global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out mice on a high fat diet compared to controls as measured by citrate synthase activity.

claim: Resistance to diet-induced obesity in Alk7 mutant mice is due to increased energy expenditure and enhanced mitochondrial function and lipid oxidation in adipose tissue.

claim: Activation of β-ARs by catecholamines is the major regulatory pathway of fat mobilization during starvation and exercise.
source: Activation of β-ARs by catecholamines is the major regulatory pathway of fat mobilization during starvation and exercise.

claim: Mice lacking all three types of β-ARs are massively obese on a high fat diet without an increase in food intake.

evidence: This is supported by citation to Bachman et al., 2002.

claim: β-agonist treatment induces mitochondria biogenesis in adipose tissue.

claim: β-agonist treatment reduces fat mass.
source: Conversely, β-agonist treatment induces mitochondria biogenesis in adipose tissue and reduces fat mass (Ghorbani et al., 1997), resembling the phenotype observed in Alk7 mutant mice.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ghorbani et al., 1997.

claim: β-AR-dependent fat mobilization is severely impaired during a high fat diet.

claim: Under a chow diet, injection of the β3-AR-specific agonist CL316243 enhanced lipolysis significantly more in fat-specific Alk7 knock-out mice than in wild type controls.

claim: After 16 weeks on a high fat diet, global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out mice displayed elevated lipolysis compared to controls under basal conditions.

claim: After 16 weeks on a high fat diet, global and fat-specific Alk7 knock-out mice displayed elevated lipolysis compared to controls following β3-AR stimulation.

evidence: This is supported by lipolysis assays shown in Figure 5B-C.

claim: No change in basal or agonist-stimulated lipolysis was detected in brain-specific Alk7 knock-out mice.
source: On the other hand, we detected no change in basal or agonist-stimulated lipolysis in brain-specific Alk7 knock-out mice (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by lipolysis assays shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Levels of epinephrine and norepinephrine were not significantly altered in the adipose tissue of Alk7 knock-out mice.

evidence: This is supported by catecholamine measurements shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The levels of Adrb1 and Adrb3 mRNAs were significantly protected in Alk7 knock-out mice after 16 weeks on a high fat diet.

claim: Adrb1 and Adrb3 mRNAs were barely detectable in the adipose tissue of control mice after 16 weeks on a high fat diet.
source: In agreement with this, the levels of Adrb1 and Adrb3 mRNAs were significantly protected in Alk7 knock-out mice after 16 weeks on a high fat diet, but were barely detectable in the adipose tissue of control mice (Figure 5E,F).
evidence: This is supported by Q-PCR data shown in Figure 5E-F.

claim: Expression of Rgs2 was elevated after a high fat diet in the adipose tissue of wild type mice but not in Alk7 knock-out mice.

evidence: This is supported by Q-PCR data shown in Figure 5G-I.

claim: Rgs2 is a negative regulator of adrenergic signaling and an inhibitor of adenylate cyclase.
source: In addition, expression of the negative regulator of adrenergic signaling Rgs2, an inhibitor of adenylate cyclase, was elevated after a high fat diet in the adipose tissue of wild type mice but not in Alk7 knock-out mice (Figure 5G) or fat-specific Alk7 knock-out mice (Figure 5H,I).
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about Rgs2 function.

claim: Adrb1 and Adrb3 mRNA levels were significantly higher in fat-specific Alk7 knock-outs compared to controls after a high fat diet.
source: Adrb1 and Adrb3 mRNA levels were also significantly higher in fat-specific Alk7 knock-outs compared to controls after a high fat diet (Figure 5H,I).
evidence: This is supported by Q-PCR data shown in Figure 5H-I.

claim: Increased levels of total and phosphorylated hormone-sensitive lipase were observed in the adipose tissue of Alk7 knock-out mice after 16 weeks on a high fat diet compared to wild type controls.
source: In line with enhanced adrenergic signaling, we observed increased levels of total and phosphorylated hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL), a major target of the β-adrenergic pathway in adipocytes, and phosphorylated PKA substrates in the adipose tissue of Alk7 knock-out mice after 16 weeks on a high fat diet compared to wild type controls (Figure 5J,K).

claim: HSL is a major target of the β-adrenergic pathway in adipocytes.

evidence: This is based on established knowledge about HSL function.

claim: Increased levels of phosphorylated PKA substrates were observed in the adipose tissue of Alk7 knock-out mice after 16 weeks on a high fat diet compared to wild type controls.
source: In line with enhanced adrenergic signaling, we observed increased levels of total and phosphorylated hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL), a major target of the β-adrenergic pathway in adipocytes, and phosphorylated PKA substrates in the adipose tissue of Alk7 knock-out mice after 16 weeks on a high fat diet compared to wild type controls (Figure 5J,K).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5J-K.

claim: Norepinephrine injection induced a more pronounced increase in PKA activity in the adipose tissue of Alk7 knock-out mice than in control mice.

evidence: This is an inference based on the collective data from knockout mice.

claim: Cell-autonomous ALK7 signaling in adipose tissue suppresses β-adrenergic signaling under a high fat diet.
source: Together, these data suggest that cell-autonomous ALK7 signaling in adipose tissue suppresses catecholamine sensitivity and β-adrenergic signaling under a high fat diet.
evidence: This is an inference based on the collective data from knockout mice.

claim: Stimulation of wild type adipocytes with activin B reduced expression of Hsl mRNA.

claim: Activin B had no effect on adipocytes derived from Alk7 knock-out MEFs.

claim: The effects of activin B on adipocyte gene expression are mediated by ALK7.

claim: Activin B downregulated expression of mRNA encoding PPARγ in wild type adipocytes.

claim: Activin A had no significant effect on Adrb2, Adrb3, and Hsl mRNA levels in wild type adipocytes.

claim: ALK7 adenovirus-mediated overexpression leads to ligand-independent receptor activation.

claim: ALK7 is sufficient to suppress β-AR expression in adipocytes.

claim: An analogue-sensitive kinase allele of Alk7 was engineered by mutation of two residues in the active site of the ALK7 kinase.

An analogue-sensitive kinase allele of Alk7 (termed Alk7ASKA) was engineered by mutation of two residues in the active site of the ALK7 kinase.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method used.

claim: Substitution of the 'gatekeeper' residue Ser270 with Gly creates an extra pocket in the ALK7 active site.
source: Substitution of the 'gatekeeper' residue Ser270 with Gly creates an extra pocket in the ALK7 active site, which can be further expanded by mutating the adjacent residue Leu250 to Val.
evidence: This is based on knowledge about kinase structure and the chemical-genetic approach.

claim: The mutations in Alk7ASKA had no effect per se on ligand-mediated signaling.

claim: The mutations in Alk7ASKA rendered the mutant receptor sensitive to inhibition by ATP competitive inhibitors, such as 2NaPP1.
source: As assessed in transfected cells, the mutations had no effect per se on ligand-mediated signaling, but rendered the mutant receptor sensitive to inhibition by ATP competitive inhibitors, such as 2NaPP1 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assay and Western blot data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: 2NaPP1 treatment did not affect signaling by the wild type ALK7 receptor.
source: 2NaPP1 treatment did not affect signaling by the wild type ALK7 receptor (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assay and Western blot data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Alk7ASKA mice developed normally.

claim: Alk7ASKA mice displayed normal growth.

claim: 1NaPP1 is an isomer of 2NaPP1 with established in vivo stability.

claim: Residual activin B activity in Alk7ASKA adipocytes treated with 1NaPP1 was likely due to expression of the related receptor ALK4.

claim: ALK4 can respond to activin B by activating Smad3.
source: Residual activin B activity in Alk7ASKA adipocytes treated with 1NaPP1 was likely due to expression of the related receptor ALK4, which can also respond to activin B by activating Smad3.

claim: Alk7ASKA and wild type mice gained weight at the same rate on a high fat diet, increasing by approximately 4 g by the end of the second week.

claim: Injection of 1NaPP1 significantly reduced the weight gain rate in Alk7ASKA mice on a high fat diet.

claim: 1NaPP1 had no effect on weight gain in wild type mice.

claim: Acute disruption of ALK7 signaling can protect adult mice from diet-induced obesity.

claim: Treatment with 1NaPP1 enhanced induction of lipolysis by the β3-AR-specific agonist CL316243 in adipose tissue biopsies extracted from Alk7ASKA mice.

claim: Acute disruption of ALK7 signaling in adult mice can uncouple nutrient overload from catecholamine resistance in adipose tissue.

claim: Obesity induces catecholamine resistance in adipose tissue by interfering with downstream β-adrenergic signaling pathways, such as PKA activity.

evidence: This is supported by citations to Reynisdottir et al., 1994; Arner, 1999; Jocken et al., 2008.

claim: ALK7 functions homeostatically in adult adipocytes to regulate catecholamine sensitivity in response to the diet.
source: Our studies in fat-specific Alk7 knock-out mice and Alk7ASKA knock-in mice demonstrate that ALK7 functions cell-autonomously and homeostatically in adult adipocytes to regulate catecholamine sensitivity in response to the diet.
evidence: This is an inference based on the acute inhibition experiments showing effects in adult mice.

claim: Adipocytes lacking ALK7 retain significant levels of β-AR expression and adrenergic signaling, allowing sustained lipid catabolism and increased energy expenditure.
source: Adipocytes lacking ALK7 retain significant levels of β-AR expression and adrenergic signaling, allowing sustained lipid catabolism and increased energy expenditure.

claim: Activin B and adenovirus-mediated ALK7 overexpression suppressed β-agonist stimulated lipolysis in human adipocytes, suggesting functional conservation of the ALK7 signaling pathway in human diet-induced obesity.
source: The fact that activin B and adenovirus-mediated ALK7 overexpression suppressed β-agonist stimulated lipolysis in human adipocytes suggests functional conservation of the ALK7 signaling pathway in human diet-induced obesity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the human adipocyte data.

claim: A high fat diet and obesity increase adipocyte expression of the two main ALK7 ligands activin B and GDF-3.
source: A high fat diet and obesity increase adipocyte expression of the two main ALK7 ligands activin B and GDF-3 (Witthuhn and Bernlohr, 2001; Sjöholm et al., 2006; Hoggard et al., 2009), suggesting enhanced ALK7 signaling in obesity.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Witthuhn and Bernlohr, 2001; Sjöholm et al., 2006; Hoggard et al., 2009.

claim: Diet-induced obesity elevates the level of activated phospho-Smad3 in mouse adipose tissue.
source: In line with this, diet-induced obesity elevates the level of activated phospho-Smad3 in mouse adipose tissue (Yadav et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yadav et al., 2011.

claim: Mouse and human Alk7 mRNA expression is highest in adipose tissue.

evidence: This is supported by citations to Kang and Reddi, 1996; Rydén et al., 1996; Carlsson et al., 2009; Murakami et al., 2012.

claim: Modulation of ALK7 signaling may offer an alternative approach to regulate catecholamine sensitivity and β-adrenergic signaling specifically and selectively in adipose tissue.
source: Thus, modulation of ALK7 signaling may offer an alternative approach to regulate catecholamine sensitivity and β-adrenergic signaling specifically and selectively in adipose tissue.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal based on the tissue-specific expression pattern and experimental findings.

claim: ALK7 represents a novel link between nutrient overload and catecholamine resistance in adipose tissue.
source: We propose that ALK7 represents a novel link between nutrient overload and catecholamine resistance in adipose tissue, and suggest that strategies to suppress ALK7 signaling may be beneficial to combat human obesity.
evidence: This is a proposal based on the collective experimental findings.
